notes: TURBO release. EC0 File Buddy now drives MTExec directly through its own Windows commands instead of screen searches and keystrokes: about 3 to 4 seconds per site instead of about 15, the same on every machine, monitor setup and display scaling. Every step is checked against MTExec, Bellevue masks are verified before they're kept, and any MTExec that doesn't match falls back to the classic method by itself. Required update.

changes: TURBO. EC0 File Buddy now drives MTExec directly with MTExec's own Windows commands, the same messages its buttons send. No screen searches, no keystrokes, no mouse moves, and nothing has to be on screen or in focus. A regular site takes about 3 to 4 seconds instead of about 15, and display scaling, monitor layout and window position no longer matter.
There is one speed now: Turbo. The speed slider is gone.

Every step is checked against MTExec before the next one. The EC0 file has to show up in the dataset list, the Time button has to show exactly the target dates, and the report has to be fully built before it is saved. A saved file that comes out incomplete is deleted and the site is flagged, so a half-built report is never left behind.

Reports are the same as the classic method's (compared line by line on real Bellevue sites). Also tested on real data: one-way in both directions, Cities speed limits, twin sets, every date option, date moves across a month boundary, and a first day the data only partly covers.

Bellevue .1 reports: the exclusion mask is set directly, and the saved file's header has to show exactly Monday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday excluded. A wrong one is deleted and redone. This also fixes the Bellevue failure at the Clear All step on laptops.

Safe on other MTExec versions. Before sending MTExec a command, the app confirms from that MTExec's own resources that the command means what Turbo expects, and every button and box is found by its label or contents, not a fixed position. If anything about an MTExec install doesn't match, the app switches that run to the classic method by itself.

If MTExec has a window open when a site starts (for example a New report someone started by hand), it is restarted clean first. If MTExec gets stuck partway through a report, the site errors within seconds instead of hanging, and the next site gets a fresh MTExec.
If a Bellevue step fails, the open MTExec dialogs are cancelled and MTExec restarts cleanly before the next site.
Google Sheet status updates run in the background, so they no longer hold up the next site.

Individual and NS0 reports (still on the classic method) press the toolbar Save and Local profile buttons directly instead of searching the screen for them, and the Datasets Next button is pressed directly on every path. That removes a pause of about 4 seconds per site on some laptops.

Mandatory updates. From this version on, the app checks the minimum supported version before it processes. If yours is older, it shows an Update required window with a Download button and won't process until you update. If the update server can't be reached, it doesn't block you.
New supercharged logo and Turbo look.

MTExec now always opens on the primary monitor. MTExec remembers the screen position it was last closed at (in its own Windows registry entry) and reopens there on every launch, including the relaunches the app does mid-run for restarts and error recovery. Dock or undock a laptop and that remembered spot can land on a second monitor, half off-screen, or too big for the screen. Before every launch the app now checks that remembered position and, if it is not fully on the primary monitor, moves it there and un-minimizes it. The 'open MTExec on your primary display first' ritual is no longer needed.

Every MTExec window the automation touches (Datasets, Load data file, Report vortex, Time range, Save report, and the rest) is pulled onto the primary monitor and restored from minimized the moment the app activates it. Image recognition can only see the primary monitor, so a dialog that drifted to a second screen was invisible to it before.

Window activation no longer trips over the Windows foreground lock. When a plain activate is refused, the app uses the thread-attach trick and then the Alt+Tab switch path, and only gives up after all three. A refused activate was a likely cause of 'the file loaded but nothing happened next' on fleet laptops.

The Next button on the Datasets window has a second method: if the image match fails, the app clicks the real Windows button control directly (no mouse, no screenshot, no template, works on any monitor and at any DPI), then falls back to the keyboard as before. The three separate copies of this logic (regular, individual, and NS0 flows) are now one shared routine.
Window lookups prefer windows that belong to MTExec.exe. A browser tab or Teams window whose title happened to contain 'Datasets' or 'MTExec' could be picked over the real dialog.
If the primary-monitor image search misses and more than one monitor is attached, the app searches every monitor and uses the match, but only if that spot belongs to an MTExec window.

The template matcher always tries the common Windows scale ratios (67%, 80%, 125%, 150%), so a laptop docked to a 100% external monitor still matches templates that were captured at 125%, and the other way round when undocked.
The startup log and every MTExec launch now record the full monitor layout (count, positions, sizes, per-monitor DPI), so multi-monitor reports can be diagnosed from a pasted log.

Fixed a wrong month bug in the Site Parameters table when a begin date crosses into the next month. With a set date of 8/30, nudging the begin date to 'Tue 01' (Sep 01) recomputed the end date as if the begin were Aug 01, showing 'Tue 04' instead of 'Fri 04', and further nudges drifted the same way. The table's date parsing now uses the same weekday-aware month inference as processing, so 'Tue 01' can only mean the month where the 1st is actually a Tuesday.

Date adjustments are now VERIFIED silently: after clicking the day arrows the app reads the date box's text directly through Windows (no mouse movement, no clicking back, about a millisecond) and confirms it shows the target date. If a machine's controls don't answer that query, a one-time visible read-back on the first adjusted site covers it. If clicks don't land, the app hunts through candidate arrow positions, verifies each with a read, locks in the one that works for the rest of the run, and corrects the date. If the box still can't be brought to the target it errors loudly instead of silently saving a report with the wrong date range.

Begin/end date boxes are located by their fixed proportions of the Time range window instead of dead-reckoning from the Auto-Wrap dropdown, so the cursor lands on the right box on every machine and DPI. Every click that precedes a read is also focus-verified: if the click didn't land inside the control that has keyboard focus, it counts as a miss, so a stale read can never grab the previous box's text.

Manual mode sets Auto Wrap via keyboard navigation FIRST (instant, verified via Windows that it is on an actual dropdown), with image match as backup. Kills the 5-15 second pause at the Time range window on every machine, and the fallback can no longer grab the wrong control or flip Auto Wrap to 'Aligned weeks'.

Image recognition tries every bundled template variant (standard, _Helix, _pc) on every machine, best guess first, instead of betting on machine detection. Fixes fleet laptops whose Windows setup never says 'helix' and removes the 5s stall before Next on the Datasets window.

Manual date reading is self-correcting: if the cursor misses the begin/end date textbox, the app probes nearby spots until a real date comes back and logs the offset. If nothing is found it saves a debug screenshot to logs/ instead of failing blind.

The date read keystrokes are only sent when a text box actually has focus, with the Ctrl key held using explicit timing. On laggy machines a dropped Ctrl could send a bare 'a' into the Auto-Wrap dropdown and cycle it through the Aligned entries.

Much smarter machine detection: BIOS hardware model (the fleet's Dell Pro 16 Plus is recognized directly), battery check for laptop vs desktop, plus the old environment check. The startup log prints the full machine profile (detection result and why, hardware model, laptop or not, screen size) so machine-specific reports are diagnosable from a pasted log.
The app window now opens at 92% of the screen (capped at 1720x1080), so laptops open near-full without the scroll-and-maximize dance.

Picking the wrong folder level warns immediately: selecting the EC0/NS0 folder itself, or a pickup-date folder like 'Pickup 7-24', pops a reminder to select the ROOT project folder that contains the EC0 folder.
New install-location check on startup: if the app isn't running from inside C:\IDAX it warns you, and if that folder doesn't exist it offers to create it.
MTExec relaunch after an error now waits up to 25s (was 10s) for slow cold starts on fleet laptops.
The version badge in the top-left of the app always shows the real version now (it was a second hand-edited copy stuck at 1.4.0; both it and the footer come from the app itself).

Fixed a wrong-month date inference bug on long studies. When the end date sat about as many days after the set date as the same day number sat before it (a 15-day gap tie), the app could read e.g. 'Wed 22' as Jun 22 instead of Jul 22 and click the date 23 days in the wrong direction. Date inference now uses the weekday name shown next to the day number to pin down the month, floors end dates at the set date (no data can exist before the tubes went in), and breaks any remaining tie toward the later date.

Multi-week study support: Study Length now accepts 14, 21, and 28 days. Studies longer than 7 days are automatically processed as weekly report passes in a single run (e.g. a 14-day study set 7/7 processes Jul 08 to Jul 15, then Jul 15 to Jul 22), each pass loading the same EC0 file(s) and adjusting the time range to its own week.

Weekly passes run in rounds: week 1 for every site first, then MTExec restarts and week 2 runs for every site, and so on. MTExec crashes if the same EC0 file is loaded twice in one session, so each round gets a fresh instance.
The MTExec restart sequence (used for error recovery, the 25-site limit, the individual-report phase, and now week rounds) was five copy-pasted blocks; it is now one shared routine.

Weekly pass reports save with a week suffix on the processing name, '_Week 1' and '_Week 2' by default (e.g. '1_Main St NB_Week 1'). Each week's suffix is editable right in the WEEKS row, and APPLY TO ALL copies both the dates and the names to matching sites. The tracker sheet status only flips to READY TO PROCESS after the final week's pass saves.

Weekly passes force Manual date processing even if an aligned-days option is selected globally, since those shortcuts would ignore the per-week date ranges and produce identical reports for every week.
Odd lengths split cleanly too: a 10-day study runs as a 7-day pass plus a 3-day pass.

New week schedule editor: multi-week sites show a WEEKS row right in the Site Parameters table with each weekly pass auto-calculated (Wk1 7/08 to 7/15, Wk2 7/15 to 7/22, ...). Every date has arrow nudgers and accepts typed dates like 7/18, for when tubes failed mid-study and got reset. Moving a week's begin slides the whole week; moving its end stretches it and drags any later chained weeks along, while weeks you have deliberately decoupled stay put. Includes AUTO/CUSTOM badge, RESET back to auto, and APPLY TO ALL to copy the schedule to every site with the same study length.
Week passes edited in the schedule editor carry exact dates into processing, so no month guessing happens at all for those adjustments.
Fixed the per-site Study Length dropdown listing only 1-7 (the column options pushed from Python were overriding the new list).

Fixed date adjustment arrow detection during manual time range processing. The search zone was looking in the wrong spot relative to the date box, so the app paused on every site while the image search timed out before falling back. The zone is now anchored to the day arrows' actual position, the match is instant, and the per-site pause is gone.

Added per-machine image template support: the app now auto-prefers <name>_pc.png captures on ultrawide / high-res monitors and keeps preferring _Helix variants on Helix laptops. Applied to the left/right date arrows and the report profile labels.

Custom reports profile selection now image-matches the profile row (ALL STATS / SPEED STATS) inside a zone around the expected row and picks the nearest match, so rows sharing a label prefix can't be confused. The known-good fixed coordinate is kept as a fallback.
Activity Log text can now be highlighted and copied with the mouse, and a new Copy button copies the entire log to the clipboard in one click.
Image-rec diagnostics: when an arrow match fails, the app now saves a debug screenshot to logs/ and records the best correlation score, so template mismatches can be diagnosed instead of guessed at.
Complete UI overhaul: switched from Tkinter to a modern HTML interface running in pywebview. Cleaner look, better proportions, more responsive on every machine.

Site Parameters table rebuilt with fixed pixel widths so headers and cells stay aligned regardless of DPI or screen size. Added a column-hover glow effect and refined inline editors for dates, checkboxes, and dropdowns.
Added Recents dropdowns next to the Project Tracker URL and Project Folder fields. Trackers show the actual sheet name, not just the URL. Persists across launches.
New 'Get Started' stepper at the top walks through Load Tracker -> Load Folder -> Set Study Length -> Scan Files. Auto-hides once everything is set up.
Reworked the during-processing error prompt: 10-second countdown with Stop / Retry / Skip to Next buttons. Pops to the front of MTExec so it's actually visible. Auto-skips on timeout.
Site processing loops now support retry. Picking Retry reattempts the same site up to 3 times before moving on.
Cross-machine cursor reliability: mouse moves now verify their position via Win32 before clicking. Fixes the 'click fires before mouse arrives' issue on slower laptops.
Image recognition got a multi-scale fallback: if the standard match fails, it retries the template at 0.875x through 1.125x to handle DPI / font-scaling differences across machines.
Fixed the Date Processing dropdown so it actually populates the right options when you change study length.

Security hardening: credentials are encrypted on disk via Windows DPAPI after first launch (plaintext is wiped). All Python dependencies pinned to exact versions. External CDN references for fonts and icons removed (everything ships locally now). Input validation added across the JS-to-Python bridge.

Build hardening: only known file types get bundled (no stray dev files in releases), the .exe carries proper version metadata, UPX compression disabled (was triggering AV false positives), and the build script validates the version string before using it in shell.
Bundle trimming: dropped 85MB of unused Google API discovery JSONs, switched to opencv-python-headless, slimmed the bundled creature images.

Fixed an issue involving date adjustment when processing data on manual date processing. The # of days to adjust was sometimes_not calculating correctly when the data spanned multiple months. It should now always calculate the correct # of days to adjust.

Refined CA EC0 filename parsing: if the first token is 3–5 letters and not 'BOX', use it as the box id (e.g., 'BRIG', 'GULF', 'NOVA'); if the name starts with 'BOX', use the next token; also recognizes embedded 'BOX <alnum> 0' anywhere in the name.
Dual-candidate matching: tries both the 3–5 letter code and the numeric/D-series token after 'BOX' (e.g., 'BRIG' and '56') so California projects match reliably regardless of tracker convention.

UI: Added 'Reset (Clear All)' button in the Action Buttons row (after Stop, before Help) to reinitialize the app—clears loaded tracker & project folder, wipes Site Parameters, resets internal flags, and empties Status.
Minor UI fixes: made it so entries on the site parameters frame will better stay aligned with their headers.

Stability polish: safer stop/cleanup of worker state on reset; clears pause/stop events; extra guards for missing/cleared widgets; scrollregion refresh for Site Parameters after table clears; slightly clearer status messages during reset.
Updated file matching logic: Now intelligently handles California's 4-letter box names (TYPE, TOMB, PLAN, GOWN, etc.) and inconsistent naming formats.
Enhanced box extraction: If filename starts with 'BOX', takes the word after it; otherwise takes the first word. Handles all state formats seamlessly.
Expanded EC0 folder detection: Now searches for 'ec0', 'ECO', 'EC0 Files', 'ECO Files' and all case variations, making setup more flexible.
Responsive UI improvements: Added vertical resizing for Status and Site Parameters sections, scrollable main controls, and better small-screen support.
Removed unused Study Days checkboxes to simplify interface and eliminate confusion.
Fixed layout issues where controls were hidden on smaller screens - now fully accessible via scrolling and resizable panes.
Public Rollout Build: Major stability and performance overhaul to ensure a smooth experience across all office machines.
Significantly improved the smoothness and reliability of the Cities/Speed processing mode.
Refined UI feedback and internal logging to better capture performance metrics and potential hangs.
Future Work Focus: Continued speed enhancements, resolving minor file-loading lag on some systems, and collaborating with other offices to develop new, client-specific processing types.
